newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian commander complains of NATO harassment.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian commander complains of NATO harassment.

text.p: NATO forces stopped a car carrying Bosnian army commander General Rasim Delic at a checkpoint west of Sarajevo on Thursday, checking it and his bodyguards for contraband weapons, NATO said.
The incident took place on the same day NATO troops confiscated all the weapons from a brigade under Delic's control for violating the Dayton peace accord.
Major Brett Boudreau, a spokesman for NATO-led peace forces in Sarajevo, denied any connection between the two actions and insisted there was no attempt to harass Delic.
But NATO did issue a press release announcing its top two officers in Bosnia had apologised to Delic for delaying him.
"We have the right under Dayton to search for illegal weapons and we do it all the time," the spokesman told Reuters.
"Our troops didn't even realize at first who they were dealing with. There is certainly no connection between that search and the confiscation of weapons at the brigade headquarters outside Celic."
Delic accused NATO of orchestrating pressure on Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic, who spent Thursday in Paris attending an international conference on the future of the Dayton peace process.
He complained that NATO paid far more attention to him and his car on Thursday than it has to scores of indicted war criminals in Bosnia, none of whom it has so far arrested.
"Weapons were pointed at me and my associates ranging from sniper rifles to anti-aircraft machine guns on three armoured personnel carriers," Delic said on the government's evening radio broadcast.
"I asked that (NATO's) command be called on the telephone. Either they did not do it or they did it very slowly because I was there for 45 minutes."
Delic said that when he finally tired of waiting for permission to pass and decided to drive on, NATO soldiers kicked his car, smashing some parts.

"I regard this as a provocation considering everything they are not doing on the other (Serb) side because (former Serb army chief Ratko) Mladic and other war criminals walk by them and they do not react," Delic said in the broadcast.
The Dayton peace agreement which ended 43 months of fighting in Bosnia last year calls for the arrest of all those indicted for war crimes by a U.N. tribunal, including Mladic.
NATO has refused to track down the indictees, vowing only to arrest them if they are encountered in the course of ordinary NATO duties.
